bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/control.rs, springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs, springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs, springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs, springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs, tools/app-control.py
summary: Scripting Bridge drives other apps by sending Apple events to their sdef-described scripting interface, with generated Objective-C proxies. BifrOSt has no Apple-event or sdef layer and no generated proxies. Its nearest counterpart is a per-app JSON-RPC control socket that only the same user can reach, plus a workspace API for launching and watching apps. The pure scripting model in springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs adds a machine-readable dictionary of classes, typed properties with access, element arrays with lookup by name, id or position, and a per-target last error with a failure delegate. Apps do not yet publish that model through their control socket, so callers still see only named methods.

features.feature: Attach to a running scriptable app (SBApplication init by bundle id, pid or URL)
features.note: A running app can be listed and its socket found (tools/app-control.py list). There is no handle object for a target app; a caller addresses it by app id and gets the socket path.

features.feature: Launch and activate a target app
features.note: open_with starts an installed app by id. Launch flags and an explicit activate call are not exposed. workspace.rs states that nothing there launches a binary.

features.feature: Scripting class mapping from a dictionary (sdef) to generated proxies
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs (Dictionary, Class, Dictionary::describe_xml); App::rpc_methods in springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs
features.note: A dictionary model lists classes, properties (type and access) and element arrays, and describes them as XML text. No client proxy classes are generated, and no app publishes its dictionary through the control socket yet. Callers still read each app's method list at runtime (app.methods).

features.feature: Properties and elements (get, set, property(withCode:), elementArray(withCode:))
features.apple: SBObject property(withCode:), property(with:code:), elementArray(withCode:), setTo(_:), get()
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs (Target::get, Target::set, Target::children, Object::property, Object::children); springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (method dispatch via handle(method, params))
features.note: Target reads declared properties and writes writable ones, checking access and kind against the dictionary. Apps must still route their control methods through it; the notes app serves named reads (notes.list, notes.get) and does not use the model yet.

features.feature: Element arrays with lookup by name, id or index, and per-element filtering
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs (Locator::Name, Locator::Id, Locator::Index, Step paths); springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (EntityQuery: entity.query with suggested, ids or string)
features.note: Lookup by name, id and 0-based position works along nested paths. There is no per-element message mapping (array(byApplying:)) and the index base is 0 where the official text does not state one.

features.feature: Error reporting per object and per application (lastError, eventDidFail delegate)
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs (Target::last_error, Target::on_error, ScriptError, ErrorKind); springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (RpcError::new, with_reason, JSON-RPC error reply in handle_line)
features.note: The last error is kept per target (the application), cleared by a successful call, and passed to a failure delegate once per failure. It is not kept per object, so an object cannot report its own last error.
A handler can defer its reply and set a timeout on the pending call. There is no per-app send mode setting and no equivalent of the Apple event send modes.

features.apple: Apple event descriptors bridged to Cocoa objects through the Scripting Bridge runtime
features.bifrost: none; the wire format is JSON-RPC 2.0 over an owner-only Unix socket (springboard/sdk/src/control.rs, SO_PEERCRED check)
features.note: Apple events and OSA are Apple-only transports with no equivalent here. The JSON-RPC socket covers the same job of controlling one app from another.

gaps: No generated client proxies for a dictionary and no app publishes its dictionary through the control socket yet; callers depend on each app's method list at runtime.
The generic property and element model in springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs is not wired into any app's control methods, so apps still serve named read methods only.
Last-error state is kept per application target only, not per object, and there is no failure delegate on the control socket itself.
No element filtering (array(byApplying:)) and no per-element message mapping.
The control socket accepts only the owning user (SO_PEERCRED), so one app cannot script another app that runs under a different account.
No explicit activate or launch-flag options when a caller starts an app; open_with only starts an installed app by id.
